input: Rewrite the supplied brief as one short English paragraph in Wilco's professional voice. Keep every fact. Brief: an internal coding agent produced 14 commits in 6 hours; 41 tests passed; its first deployment attempt failed because the release token was read-only; a human changed no code; the remaining risk is that the test fixtures cover only one customer configuration.
target: Score both texts from 1 to 5. A 5 opens with the result, preserves all numbers and causes, explains why the failed deployment matters, names the fixture limitation, uses plain B2 English, varies sentence length, and avoids sales language. A 1 loses facts, oversells autonomy, or hides the failure and limitation.

metadata.known_good: The agent produced 14 commits in 6 hours, and all 41 tests passed. Its first deployment still failed because the release token was read-only. Good. The boundary worked, and no human changed the code to make the result look cleaner. The limit is less interesting but more important: the fixtures cover one customer configuration, so this is evidence for that path, not for the whole product.
metadata.known_bad: In today's ever-evolving landscape, the agent delivered a robust and seamless transformation with 14 commits and 41 tests. This pivotal success unlocks autonomous development at scale.
